content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [article_no] and the latest [product_name] software. Is there a function block for alternating relay? I want the pumps to switch based on start and stop cycles, not on time as shown in the standard examples. My goal is to replace a standalone electromechanical alternating relay in a 2- or 3-pump setup. [user_name]
Hi, if you share more information, I am sure we can find a solution. Please clarify what you need and which example doesn't work for you. Regards, [user_name]
Hello, here is an alternating relay I want to replace: [url]. [user_name]

Hi. A pulse relay is the quick solution to your request. For a more detailed explanation, refer to the ZIP file attached; it includes two versions—one operating on Start/Stop signals and another using a switch with timer capability. This should help you get started. Greetings. [user_name]

Thank you for the help file. I have attached a file that switches the output each cycle. Is there a simpler method to do this? I searched for alternating relay and discovered it's also called multiplexing; another programmable relay manufacturer offers a function block with two outputs that can toggle between them. [user_name]

[user_name], your design is quite interesting—I had to draw it out to confirm that the XOR was essential! I've attached a simpler design. The dot on the block is an invert function; previously, we had to use the NOT block for inversion. You can add the dot by double-clicking the input port while in wire connect mode. Greetings. [user_name]
I suspected there was an easier way; thanks for the tip on inverting the connector.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is looking for a function block within [product_name] software to implement alternating relay logic for pump control based on start/stop cycles rather than time. While a similar functionality (multiplexing) is straightforward in competitor programmable relays, in [company_name]'s [product_name], users need to manually build the logic using basic blocks. Community members offered guidance and simpler solutions using XOR and inversion, highlighting a higher learning curve for achieving this functionality in [company_name] software compared to other brands with dedicated blocks.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to include an easy, built-in function block for alternating relay logic based on start/stop cycles, similar to what competitor programmable relay products offer.
